segments.speaker: echo
segments.text: That's Mars. You hear the wind? Perseverance recorded it a couple years ago. First time anyone heard wind on another planet. And that wreckage down there — the, umm, crumpled up metal in the crater — that's Perseverance's descent stage.

segments.speaker: echo
segments.text: Brutal. They call it the sky crane. Came in at about twelve thousand miles an hour. Burned off the heat shield, popped the parachute, and then it did this incredible thing: hovered sixty feet above the ground and lowered the actual rover down on cables. Super gently. The second the rover's wheels touched dirt, the sky crane cut the lines, flew off to the side, and crashed on purpose so it wouldn't hit the rover.

segments.speaker: echo
segments.text: That was its whole job. Seven minutes. And the reason there's a little helicopter flying around on Mars right now. First powered flight on another planet. Not bad for a crash.
